_about: The carbon estimate's constants, in one place. webapp/js/ai-footprint.js carries the same numbers for the Rubicon page and tests/rubicon-footprint-twin.test.mjs fails if the two disagree. km_examples are the distances and how both ends say them. Each figure is named with its source; see footprint.py for how they are combined.
high_source: Simon P. Couch, 'Electricity use of AI coding agents', 20 January 2026, https://simonpcouch.com/blog/2026-01-20-cc-impact/: about 390 Wh per million input tokens and 1,950 per million output tokens for Claude Opus, back-solved from Epoch AI's estimate for a 100,000-token prompt with output at five times the input rate, as Anthropic's prices are. The author calls them napkin maths.
low_source: Oviedo et al., 'Energy use of AI inference, efficiency pathways, and test-time scaling', arXiv:2509.20241: a median 0.31 Wh per query for frontier models, and widely cited estimates overstated by 4 to 20 times. The low case takes the high case's rates divided by the top of that range.
overhead_source: Our assumption, not a measurement: an agent re-sends its instructions, earlier turns and tool output with every request, so it reads far more than the documents themselves. The low case counts only what was read and written; the high case counts what was read ten times over.
grid_source: DESNZ greenhouse gas reporting conversion factors, UK grid electricity, 2024.
car_source: DESNZ greenhouse gas reporting conversion factors, average car of unknown fuel, 2024.
